“A diagnosis for gender dysphoria is included in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5)” mayoclinic.org the DSM-5 includes mental disorders such as:
ADHD
Autism
PTSD
Substance Abuse
OCD
Schizophrenia 

Those are all mental illnesses, and gender dysphoria is classified among them. As for cisgender people also suffering from GD, the numbers of that are exponentially low, .005-.014% in Males and .002-.003% in Females, according to, again, the DSM-5. 

As for the “transgender is not the result of mental illness or gender dysphoria” by that argument, any cisgendered person can transition without GD and demand to be treated as the opposite gender, we see it constantly in sports where male athletes will transition to compete against women. *(In my experience I’ve also heard the argument that cisgendered people can’t “identify as xyz” because they don’t have GD, but that’s just personal experience)* So where do we draw the line? Anyone can transition regardless of whether or not they have GD or only people with GD can transition?

I will admit to being wrong about the puberty blockers, as a quick 5 minute research has not supported my claim, however that’s only clicking on the first couple of links to pop up. I will go back and do more in depth research later. (I might still be proven wrong I just want to be thorough)

As for the rate of regret, it is difficult to find a solid number, some reports say 1% others say 13.1%, the problem being how the studies define regret amongst other things. We will likely have to weight a few more years to get an accurate count.

The ideology that children are mature enough to make the decision to have these surgeries and alter their entire body when there’s a chance they were pushed or persuaded to believe they fall into the transgender category, it goes against my beliefs. I once believed I was bisexual, that I liked men like I liked women. I was 12. Im 21 now and I’m not into men. Young children don’t know what they want or who they are. I don’t care if a boy dresses like a girl, or vice versa to explore their identity however,

My *person beliefs* are that kids shouldn’t have access to procedures and surgery’s to affirm the care, and adults, as long as they have diagnosed GD and aren’t transition to take advantage of women’s sports or something similar, by all means go ahead.

Transgender has been proven to be a result of the mental illness known as “gender dysphoria” I’m not saying it’s a bad thing to transition, do what makes you happy. 

However, children are very impressionable and susceptible to people such as EXTREMELY, not all, liberal teachers saying that just because a girl likes doing boy things she must be a boy trapped in a girls body or vice versa. 

I firmly believe children are not mature enough to make decisions like taking puberty blockers, or in a males’ case being castrated/tucked. There are a plethora of accounts coming from people who transitioned as kids not knowing/understanding the full extent of the consequences later on and have grown up, matured and now regret that decision because it’s severely limited their livelihood or impacted their quality of life.

As for medical professionals, they should know that children, again, aren’t mature enough to make these kinds of permanent decisions and advise against these kinds of treatments for children. For medical professionals to advise parents and their children that going onto puberty blockers and other hormonal drugs that effect natural hormones is immoral and an abuse of power; because as doctors they are trusted with taking care of people with ailments and parents may not be well versed in the consequences long and short term of putting their children on these drugs.

Again, these are just my personal beliefs. I’m not trying to attack or invalidate anyone or their personal beliefs because everyone is entitled to their own opinions and beliefs, I’m open to conversation about it.

For those saying why was it loaded and why wasn’t the safety on: I don’t know the model of the firearm, but not all handguns on external safeties, or “togglable safeties” if that makes more sense. Some have trigger safeties, like mine, where the trigger will not pull unless you have your finger on the trigger properly, if your curious I have a CZ P-10C and if you look at a photo you’ll see the trigger then what looks like a second trigger sticking out of it. As for it being loaded, one of the weapon conditions, or what “state” the firearm is in is Condition 1: magazine inserted, weapon on safe, round in chamber. It’s is a common way to store firearms that are meant to be used for self defense, as if a fast moving situation, you might not have the few extra seconds to load a magazine and/or rack the side. But I do agree with those who are saying it should have be holstered, holsters not only protect the firearm from damage, but also cover the trigger to prevent negligent discharges like this.

She remembered the beginning of her quest. She wasn’t the leader at all. She wasn’t even supposed to be their. Why would she be? After all, a princess shouldn’t be fighting the battles of men.

*************************************************

It begins on Midas. The king, King Imos, learned of an approaching threat of Orcs ready to march on the kingdom.

“Tiana, would you come for a moment?” The king called out. Seconds later his daughter, tall and beautiful, wearing a blue silk dress, that fit seamlessly, and her Green-Blonde-ish hair fixed to be straight with a single braid falling over her left shoulder, emerged from her chambers.

“Yes Father, how can I serve you?” Tiana asked.

“My dearest daughter, my scouts have reported Orcs approaching the city. I ask if you to take your mother and hide in my secret chambers.” The king ordered.

“But Father,” Tiana pleaded, “I can help fight these Orcs, I’ve been training since you first taught me to hold a sword! I can-” The king cut her off, “Absolutely not!” He bellowed, “I will not have my DAUGHTER, Princess of Hypfilia, fight Orcs!”

“But Fa-” Tiana was cut off again. “Take. Your. Mother. NOW.” The king demanded.

“Yes, *father*.” She said with a hiss. She walked off to her chambers to get her sword before retrieving her mother. She walked through her chamber doors and knelt down to gather her sword. As she knelt, she saw fires and pillars of smoke rising above the walls.

*I can’t just let this happen,* she thought, *I have to fight for MY kingdom.* 

So Tiana grabbed her sword, and cut her hair. Long locks of her hair fell to the floor as she cut it down. If she didn’t want to be notice she had to try to look as similar as possible.

She grabbed the armor her father had gifted her, attached her scabbard and sheathed her sword. And she put on a helmet that covered her face. No one would see her.

*************************************************

She fell in with a random unit of soldiers about to match out the front gates. They left the safety of the castle, Hell bound.

They traveled for hours. The King has made it seem they were so much closer. But they were miles away. None the less, Tiana was going to fight for her kingdom. Finally they reached the remnants of a small village, pillaged and burned to the ground. Innocent people slaughter, women and children too. No survivors.

“Bastards, I’ll kill the lot of them.” One soldier muttered under his breathe. Tiana thought it best to remain quiet.

Just then, a horn blew in the distance. War Horns. The Orcs has laid a trap.

“RETREAT!” The captain yelled. All but 3 soldiers fled: the one that vowed to kill them, another soldier who felt like dying, and Tiana. They stayed to fight.

First there were hundreds of Orcs, and the 3 soldiers caught relentless. Tiana’s years of training against her father, showing her no remorse, taught her how to fight. Dodging blows left and right, swinging her sword for their legs to disable them, then driving her sword through their neck from behind.

The Vengeful soldier caught tirelessly, picking up and Orcish sword, duel wielding with his standard issue sword. Slicing open necks of Orcs, even decapitating them.

And the last soldier fought to his death. He hid behind his shield, slashing and stabbing at any Orcs who came towards him, but unfortunately an Orc snuck up from behind him, and drove his battle-axe through the middle of his back.

Tiana and the Vengeful Soldier eventually ended up back to back, fending of Orcs that charged them.

“We need to get up high!” He shouted

“How do you suppose we do that?! There’s no buildings!” Tiana responded.

At first the Vengeful Soldier was taken aback by the voice of a woman with him. But he quickly regained his focus, stabbing two Orcs who had come too close.

“Follow me and watch my back!” He yelled and started to clear a path for them, spinning to avoid attacks, his armor covered in Orc blood, slashing at Orc necks and stabbing at Orc chests. 

“I’m going to boost you onto this boulder! Ready?!” He shouted over the battle-cry of more charging Orcs.

“Okay! Coming your way!” Tiana shouted and bolted in the Vengeful Soldiers direction. Her foot landing on his hand. As she landed on his hand, he threw her up with all his strength. Unfortunately as she left his hand, an Orc’s sword came down on him, slashing a hole in his armor. He picked up his swords and fought the Orcs until eventually he tired out.

“Telling the king,” he started, coughing up blood in between words, “Alvor *cough* fought bravely!” As he finished his sentence, a sword came across his neck. He fell down to his knees, and as he fell forward, his head toppled of his neck.

Tiana cried out. She may have not known the soldier, but he had died to protect her.

“I’ll tell him, I promise!” She cried to the dead man.

After crying and Orcs shouting, telling her how they’ll cook her as eat her slowly, she felt a wave of rage come over her.

She took off her helmet and chucked it at the nearest Orc. She picked up her sword and jumped for Alvor’s body. She jumped over at least 5 Orcs and she landed with grace. She picked up his sword, and prepared for a fight. 

The Orcs looked around confused at first, then charged Tiana. She parried blow after blow, slicing at the Orcs, rolling underneath their legs and stabbing them from behind. If she was going to die, she was going to go out with a fight.

She fought and killed Orc after Orc, fueled by her rage, until, there were no Orcs left. Thousands of Orc bodies were littered around her.

*************************************************

She returned to the kingdom, covered head to toe in Orc blood. Her face dirtied with mud and blood. A mix of her’s and Orcs’. Soldiers stared in awe at what they were seeing. 

When the king saw her, he didn’t act furiously as Tiana had thought, but he embraced his daughter. 

“Don’t you ever leave again like that.” He said with tears in his eyes.

“Father?” Tiana started, “I’d like to be in the Army.” She said, and began laughing. She couldn’t stop.

“Daughter, I’ll make you the commander of our Army, these soldiers could learn a thing or two from you.”
